title: The bit-to-file scaling ladder, mapped across native, Python and Creation Engine
prose: A conceptual ladder from the smallest unit of information to a file on disk, with each rung mapped into three paradigms. The ladder is sound as a teaching device and the native and Python columns are correct. The CREATION ENGINE column is not: CE has FOUR rungs where this ladder has seven, and the mapping breaks hardest at 'array' and 'matrix'. A plugin contains no arrays of records and no multi-dimensional structures. Writing the corrected column is the point -- an AI that believes a plugin holds Vec<SurfaceMaterialDef> or a 2D passability grid will write a parser that cannot succeed, and will not find out until it reads a real file.

provenance.note: the 24-byte record header and the subrecord layout, from fopdoc plus a measurement of the installed plugin
engine-derived FO4 record backing classes, offsets and static_assert sizes
BGSMaterialType at sizeof 0x80 with its real member list, which disproves three fields of the proposed design

ladder.native: bool, or one bit of a uint32
ladder.creation_engine: a named bit in a record flag field
ladder.ce_evidence: BGSMaterialType.flags is uint32 @0x7C; BGSImpactData has int8 flags @0x14 and int8 resultOverride @0x15

ladder.native: uint32_t bitfield; set with |=, test with &, clear with &= ~
ladder.creation_engine: a 32-bit flags field where individual behaviours are named bits
ladder.notes: This rung is fully correct in all three columns. Engine material and impact properties are bitmasks, not arrays of bools, which is the point worth keeping from the incoming reference.

ladder.creation_engine: a subrecord payload: 4-char type, uint16 size, then the typed bytes
ladder.ce_evidence: subrecord header is type char[4] + dataSize uint16 + payload

ladder.creation_engine: a FORM record: 24-byte header then a variable, named sequence of subrecords. NOT a tuple, and NOT a flat fixed-offset block on disk.
ladder.ce_evidence: BGSMaterialType is a FIXED 0x80 in memory, but the on-disk MATT form is header plus named subrecords. Conflating the in-memory layout with the file layout is how a parser gets written against the wrong thing.

ladder.creation_engine: DOES NOT EXIST AS A CONTAINER. Repeated same-type subrecords use either a COUNT subrecord pattern (KSIZ then KVAT) or indexed subrecords. A plugin never holds an array of records.
ladder.notes: CORRECTION. The incoming mapping called this a 1D sequence equal to a Vec. In a plugin, multiple instances of a subrecord are a counted or indexed list inside ONE record, and multiple records live in separate files resolved through load order.

ladder.creation_engine: DOES NOT EXIST IN A PLUGIN. A collision or passability grid is geometry in a mesh, and Fallout 4 mesh collision is PhysX-based, not Havok.
ladder.notes: CORRECTION. What a plugin does carry are 3x4 PROJECTION matrices (WEDR, WMAP), which are a completely different concept from a 2D grid and must not be filed under the same rung.

ladder.creation_engine: a plugin (.esm/.esp/.esl/.mod) or an archive (.ba2), or a mesh (.nif)
ladder.ce_evidence: our installed PipMonTestFacility.esp is 66 bytes: 24-byte record header, dataSize 42, 24+42=66 exactly
ladder.notes: The plugin rung carries a dimension no memory paradigm has: the MASTER and OVERRIDE chain. Which file a record comes from is part of its identity, and load order decides which wins. That is why 'an array of records' is not a thing here and 'all the materials' is not a Vec -- it is a load-ordered set of records across many files.

bitmask_practice_confirmed.verdict: CORRECT in all three paradigms, and worth indexing
bitmask_practice_confirmed.why_it_matters_here: This is the cheapest representation available in-engine. An array of bools costs a byte each; a bitmask costs one bit. On an L-IN surface where the frame budget is the constraint, that difference is the whole argument.

cross_language_alignment.corroborated: The incoming reference independently describes the same 8-byte-alignment padding this workspace measured: the proposed SurfaceMaterialDef has fields summing to 36 bytes but repr(C) lays it out at 40, because sound_category_hash is a u64.

options.cost: 8 wasted bytes per entry, no other change
options.note: safest and usually right for a table of thousands

options.choice: reorder so the u64 comes first
options.note: cheapest fix; 4+8+4+4+4+4+4 = 32 with no padding at all if ordered well
SIMD-friendly but a 33 percent increase over the natural layout; only worth it if the data is actually processed in 16-byte lanes

HAZARD: in Rust, taking a reference to a field of a packed struct is a compile error, because the reference would be unaligned. Unaligned access is also a performance trap on some targets. This is the one option that trades a correctness bug for space.

cross_language_alignment.verdict: RECOMMEND reordering. It is free, it removes the padding entirely, and it avoids both the packed-struct reference hazard and the 48-byte SIMD tax.

corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: SKYRIM. Every one of those identifiers is Havok, and Fallout 4 uses PhysX. Zero of them should be indexed for this project.
corrections_to_incoming_reference.action: rejected, and fo4docs.org was also rejected earlier for documenting Havok for FO4

corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: SSE is Skyrim; SF is Starfield. We hold and index CommonLibF4, and every FO4 fact here was derived from it.

corrections_to_incoming_reference.claimed: MATT holds friction, density and bitmasks
corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: BGSMaterialType holds breakableFXModel, parentType, havokImpactDataSet, materialName, materialID, materialColor, buoyancy, flags. There is NO friction and NO density field. Friction-like behaviour is not in the material record at all.

corrections_to_incoming_reference.claimed: Vec<SurfaceMaterialDef> is the in-file representation of all engine materials
corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: Materials are individual MATT records, each its own form, resolved through the master and override chain across files. There is no material array anywhere.

corrections_to_incoming_reference.claimed: a 2D texture or physics mask maps materials to terrain or mesh pixels
corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: Not a plugin concept. Spatial mapping lives in mesh data, PhysX-based in FO4.

corrections_to_incoming_reference.claimed: BSLightingShaderProperty links physics material IDs to visual mesh geometry
corrections_to_incoming_reference.reality: BSLightingShaderProperty is real and FO4-relevant, and IS worth indexing for the mesh side. It is a lighting/shader property, not a physics link; the physics linkage is a separate structure and remains UNDOCUMENTED for FO4.
corrections_to_incoming_reference.action: partially accepted: keep the identifier, drop the claimed physics linkage

what_to_index_from_this.item: bitmasks as the cheap in-engine representation
